newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-Hilti sees high op profit, flat net.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Hilti sees high op profit, flat net.

text.p: Hilti AG, a world leader in speciality construction equipment, on Friday said operating profit would rise strongly in 1997 after falling for two years.
Net profit for 1997 would be steady or slightly higher than the previous year's 204.2 million Swiss francs, up six percent from 1995, chief executive Pius Baschera said.
"Net profit should be at the same level as last year or slightly higher if all goes well," he told a news conference.
Based in Liechtenstein, Hilti is a leading maker of drilling and assembly machines, wall-fixing technology and construction chemicals.
Hilti sales rose 9,2 percent to 2.21 billion Swiss francs in 1996, with opertaing profit down 18.3 percent to 140.1, according to key figures for last year published in April.

Baschera said operating profit, which dropped 22 percent in 1995 due to a surging Swiss franc, had fallen again last year becuase of bad weather in Europe and North America and strong pressure on margins from tough competition

Baschera said this year's operating profit would benefit from a slight revival of world construction markets, strategic improvements and favourable currency exchange rates, including a relatively weak Swiss franc and strong dollar.
Construction volume in Hilti's main world markets dropped an overall 0.8 percent last year.
But the company's projections see construction volume this year rising by 2.8 percent in North and South America, the same in Asia and 0.8 percent in Europe, its biggle single market.
Europe, including fast growing eastern and southern markets as well as very weak Germany and Switzerland, accounted for 63 percent of 1996 sales that totalled 2.2 billion Swiss francs.
North and South America made up 22 percent and Asia another 15 percent, a Hilti statement said.
Baschera said Hilti remained open to potential acquisitions in its core business but was not interested in diversifying into other businesses.
"Our studies have shown that Hilti can be profitable in the long-term and grow faster than ourt markets," Baschera said.
To reap that potential, Baschera said Hilti had adopted a new strategy named "Champion 3K" aimed at expanding or establishing world market leadership in all of its activities.

Hilti last year spent a "two-digit figure in the millions" of Swiss francs to revamp logistics, including building new warehouses and installing new software, as part of efforts to boost competitiveness, Baschera added.
